title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
The first part finishes a statement begun on p.20 about 'parties localement fermées modérées', i.e. locally closed tame subsets in an axiomatic tame topology.

Setup (from p.20): X ⊃ Y are closed tame parts in tame relative position. C_mod(Y,X) is the set of points of X not in Y that are in tame relative position with Y. Z is the smallest closed tame set containing C_mod(Y,X); it is itself in tame position with Y.

This page adds the following. Let F be the relative frontier of Y in X (the transcription's 'fonction relative' is almost certainly 'frontière relative'). Then:
- F is closed (probably 'fermé', not 'fini') and tame.
- F is a closed tame part of Y.
- F ⊂ Z.
- F contains no isolated points of Z.
- C_mod(Y,X) = C_mod(F,Z).
So the 'tame complement' of Y in X can be computed from the frontier F inside the closure Z. This is a reduction step for building a calculus of tame differences X ∖_mod Y; see the margin remark 'Z = X ∖_mod Y' on p.20.

The second part is dated 9 June (1986). L is an ordered 'tronçon'/treillis: a poset or lattice, here a lattice of pieces of a découpage. Grothendieck puts a canonical topology on L with basis of opens:
- the open intervals ]a,b[ for a<b;
- the rays L_{<a} and L_{>b}.
The rays can be omitted when L has no least (resp. greatest) element.

He observes that for a ∈ L the singleton {a} need not be closed. When L is one of the lattices attached to a découpage, he states that b ∈ closure({a}) iff b ⊃ a, 'given the position in H'. In other words, the specialization preorder of this topology recovers the inclusion order.

The next page draws the consequences:
- The space is T0, hence embeds in its sobrification.
- He asks whether such lattices are sober.
- Segments [a,b] are not closed in general; only for total orders is the topology Hausdorff.
- He proposes an alternative topology whose closed sets are generated by the [a,b] and the rays.

The purpose is to equip the combinatorial objects ('réseaux', lattices of strata produced by découpages) with topologies so that tame-topological notions (closure, frontier, modéré differences) can be read off order-theoretically.
errors: The claim b ∈ closure({a}) ⇔ b ⊃ a does not follow for a general poset from the given basis of opens. Take b > a: a basic open ]x,y[ containing b need not contain a, since x < a may fail. So the statement depends on special properties of the découpage lattice, which Grothendieck signals only vaguely ('compte tenu position dans H'). Taken as a general statement it is a gap.
In a non-total order L_{<a} is not the complement of L_{≥a}, so the analogy with the order topology on chains breaks down. Grothendieck himself recognises this on p.22.
The relative-frontier statement is given without proof; minimality of Z and the equality C_mod(Y,X) = C_mod(F,Z) rely on unstated axioms of the tame framework.

ideas.what: Calculus of tame differences of closed tame sets via relative frontier: C_mod(Y,X) = C_mod(Fr_X Y, Z)
ideas.modern_name: frontier/closure properties of definable sets in o-minimal structures (e.g. dim Fr < dim) and stratification-based set calculus
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (o-minimality, 1984–86); Shiota; Łojasiewicz (semialgebraic/subanalytic)
ideas.where_published: Only programmatic mention of 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5

ideas.what: Interval-type topology on a lattice/poset of strata whose specialization order is inclusion (closure order)
ideas.modern_name: interval topology / Alexandrov topology on the poset of strata of a stratification; specialization preorder
ideas.usually_credited_to: Frink (interval topology, 1942), Alexandrov (1937); poset of strata in exit-path theory (MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie)

ideas.what: T0 implies embedding into sobrification; question of sobriety of lattices with their canonical topology
ideas.modern_name: sober spaces / sobrification; Priestley/spectral spaces of lattices

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches an axiomatic tame topology in which tame differences X ∖_mod Y are computed by a relative-frontier recursion. In parallel he topologizes the lattices of strata of découpages so that their specialization order recovers inclusion. This is an order-theoretic foundation for 'topologie modérée', developed independently of and simultaneously with o-minimality, and never completed or published.
missed.quote: C_{mod}(Y,X) = C_{mod}(\mathcal{F}, Z) ... (9 juin) Soit L un tronçon ordonné. (1) Topologie sur L
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an alternative, lattice/poset-based axiomatics for tame geometry that is close in spirit to the poset-of-strata viewpoint in exit-path and stratified homotopy theory. It is of historical interest for documenting how Grothendieck pursued the Esquisse tame-topology program, but the individual statements are standard.

deep.surprise_reason: These are interesting traces of Grothendieck's unpublished tame-topology program in 1986. The concrete content (frontier properties, interval topology on a poset, T0/sobriety) is standard or close to known results in o-minimality and order topology.
transcription_corrections: 'fonction relative des Y dans X' should read 'frontière relative de Y dans X'.
'F est fini' is likely 'F est fermé'; similarly 'un pr. mod. fini' is likely 'une p[artie] mod[érée] fermée' of Y.
The struck-out 'C_mod' before the displayed equation is 'Compar[er]' / 'Conséquence', not part of the formula.
'Soit L un tronçon ordonné' could also read 'treillis ordonné' (p.22 speaks of 'treillis').
'Si L est l'un des lieux d'une ... 𝒳' is uncertain; it probably reads 'l'un des treillis d'un découpage'.
